title: Topological dimension of a quasi-separated algebraic space as a supremum of local-ring dimensions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with its atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume that $X$ is quasi-separated, meaning that its diagonal $X\to X\times_SX$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests (inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact). For an algebraic space $Z$ and a point $z\in|Z|$, write $\delta_Z(z)$ for the dimension of its local ring, namely the common value $\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ for an etale morphism $W\to Z$ from a scheme and a point $w$ above $z$; $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ is the stalk of the structure sheaf. Ring dimension is [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and etale morphisms are [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $$\dim|X|=\sup_{x\in|X|}\delta_X(x),$$ where topological dimension is [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and the supremum is in $\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$, so both sides are $-\infty$ for the empty space. No quasi-compactness, Noetherian, finite-dimensionality, or equidimensionality hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $a:U\to X$ from a scheme, as provided by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Surjectivity on field-valued point classes means that every $x\in|X|$ has a preimage $u\in U$ [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family].

For completeness, the common value defining $\delta_X(x)$ is independent of its chart. Given etale scheme charts $(W,w)$ and $(V,v)$ over $x$, [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] supplies a point $t\in W\times_X V$ projecting to $w,v$. Both projections are etale scheme maps by the definition of representable etale [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply the dimension equality of [lem-sfb-etale-stalk-invariants] to each projection at $t$: $\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}=\dim\mathcal O_{W\times_X V,t}=\dim\mathcal O_{V,v}$. Taking $(W,w)=(U,u)$ yields $\delta_X(a(u))=\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}$ for all $u$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-sober] to $X$ and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] to $U$. In a sober space a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets is precisely a strict chain of specializations of their generic points (in reverse order): inclusion of the closures is equivalent to specialization, and uniqueness of generic points makes strictness equivalent to distinct points. Thus [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] computes dimension as the supremum of lengths of strict specialization chains in both spaces. By [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-etale-specializations], $a$ sends a strict chain in $U$ to a strict chain in $|X|$: continuity preserves specializations, and the noncollapse clause prevents equal adjacent images. Conversely, take a chain $x_d\leadsto\cdots\leadsto x_0$ in $|X|$, choose $u_0$ above $x_0$ by step 1, and successively apply its lifting clause to obtain $u_i\leadsto u_{i-1}$ above $x_i$. Distinct images force distinct adjacent lifts. The possible finite chain lengths therefore coincide, so $\dim|X|=\dim|U|$, including empty and unbounded cases.

source.place: Tag 0A4J, lemma-dimension-decent-space, proof; point comparisons Tags 03K6, 03IL and 03K5.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] to $U$, obtaining $\dim|U|=\sup_{u\in U}\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}$. There is no Noetherian or quasi-compactness hypothesis on this scheme comparison.

Put $D=\sup_{x\in|X|}\delta_X(x)$ and $E=\sup_{u\in U}\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}$. Step 2 gives $\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}=\delta_X(a(u))\leq D$ for every $u$, hence $E\leq D$. Conversely, for each $x$ choose $u$ above it by step 1; then $\delta_X(x)=\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}\leq E$, hence $D\leq E$. Steps 3 and 4 now give $\dim|X|=E=D$. If $X$ is empty, so is $U$, and both suprema are $-\infty$. The same upper-bound argument covers infinite dimension without any finite supremum being attained.
